{{Short description|Unary truth function in many-valued logic}}
In [[many-valued logic]] with [[linear order|linearly ordered]] [[truth value]]s, '''cyclic negation''' is a unary truth function that takes a truth value ''n'' and returns ''n''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1 as value if ''n'' is not the lowest value; otherwise it returns the highest value.

For example, let the set of truth values be {0,1,2}, let ~ denote negation, and let ''p'' be a variable ranging over truth values. For these choices, if p&nbsp;=&nbsp;0 then ~p&nbsp;=&nbsp;2; and if p&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 then ~p&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.

Cyclic negation was originally introduced by the logician and mathematician [[Emil Leon Post|Emil Post]].
